text: Replace the additive user/video/context scorer with a compact embedding-plus-MLP ranker while retaining the current request-context inputs, BCE objective, optimizer, schedule, and canonical rows.
rationale: Experiment 1 reaches GAUC 0.66891 and nDCG@5 0.53696, showing useful but limited additive signal. Nonlinear modeling could capture interactions among user, video, tab, hour, and weekday without adding any new feature family.
exact_ablation: Change only the scorer architecture from the additive lookup model to a small embedding-plus-MLP model using the identical user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday fields; keep BCE, data rows, optimizer, schedule, and checkpoint rule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Moderate positive potential, approximately +0.001 to +0.006, if nonlinear context interactions improve within-user ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Small positive potential, approximately +0.001 to +0.005, but top-five gains may be limited by overfitting sparse users and rare items.

text: Add a low-rank deep-and-cross branch to the current request-context scorer, leaving the existing additive branch and BCE training unchanged.
rationale: Request context was the only screened feature group with positive internal primary lift (+0.00221), while experiment 1 still has weak top-five performance in low-volume tabs. Explicit bounded crosses may make context-dependent user/video ordering more expressive.
exact_ablation: Add only a two-layer low-rank cross branch over the existing user_id, video_id, tab, hour, and weekday representation, concatenated with the unchanged additive output; keep BCE, optimizer, schedule, rows, and checkpoint rule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely small positive effect, approximately +0.001 to +0.005, if context changes the relative preference among a user's videos.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potentially larger than the GAUC gain, approximately -0.001 to +0.006, because useful crosses may improve the highest ranks; sparse tabs could regress.

text: Replace the additive user/video scorer with a user-video latent-factor interaction model using the existing request-context additive terms.
rationale: The current additive model cannot represent personalized user-video affinity beyond separate user and video offsets. Experiment 1 has strong warm-traffic coverage but poor rare-item performance, making a compact interaction model a targeted test of whether warm-user personalization can improve ordering.
exact_ablation: Replace only the separate user_id and video_id additive weights with 16-dimensional user-video dot-product embeddings, retaining the additive tab, hour, and weekday terms, BCE loss, optimizer, schedule, and all rows.

expected_effect.GAUC: Possible moderate lift of approximately +0.002 to +0.007 on warm users, with little benefit for cold items.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Possible positive effect of approximately +0.001 to +0.006 if affinity moves relevant videos into the top five; rare-item nDCG may decline.

text: Restore pointwise BCE on the current request-context features but use class-balanced BCE weighting based only on the training label prevalence.
rationale: The pairwise experiment reduced primary from 0.60293 to 0.60045 and produced a lower nDCG@5 of 0.53498. A calibrated pointwise objective with mild training-only class weighting is a materially different loss test that may recover broad separation without the pairwise implementation's instability.
exact_ablation: Replace only the unweighted within-user pairwise logistic loss with BCE weighted by inverse training-class frequency, normalized to mean one; retain request-context features, additive architecture, rows, optimizer, schedule, and checkpoint rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely neutral to small positive, approximately -0.001 to +0.004, because weighting may improve separation but does not directly target ranking.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to small positive, approximately -0.002 to +0.004; excessive positive weighting could over-rank noisy positives.

text: Use focal BCE instead of standard BCE to reduce the influence of already-easy impressions while preserving the current additive request-context scorer.
rationale: Experiment 1 has useful aggregate ordering but very weak rare-item and tab-specific slices. Focal weighting could direct capacity toward ambiguous impressions, although it may hurt the broad natural-distribution objective if it overemphasizes noisy examples.
exact_ablation: Replace only standard BCE with focal BCE using a fixed gamma of 1.5 and no class reweighting; keep user/video/request-context fields, additive architecture, optimizer, schedule, and checkpoint rule unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small and uncertain effect, approximately -0.002 to +0.004; difficult impressions may improve pair ordering but noise can reduce broad GAUC.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potentially positive by approximately 0.000 to +0.005 if ambiguous positives are promoted into the top five, with downside from noisy rare slices.

text: Use a top-rank-emphasized pointwise loss that weights positives and negatives by their current within-user score rank, with all weights computed inside each training batch.
rationale: Experiment 1's GAUC is 0.66891 while nDCG@5 is only 0.53696, indicating that broad ordering does not fully translate to top-five quality. A rank-focused loss directly targets the metric component currently limiting primary, but introduces optimization and stability risk.
exact_ablation: Replace only BCE with a differentiable top-rank-weighted BCE whose per-row weight is a fixed function of the row's detached within-user batch rank; keep features, additive architecture, optimizer, schedule, and rows fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Could be neutral or slightly negative, approximately -0.003 to +0.003, because emphasis on the head may sacrifice lower-rank pair ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potential positive effect of approximately +0.001 to +0.008 if the batch rank proxy aligns with official top-five ordering; it may be neutral under small or incomplete user batches.

text: Train the current BCE model with chronological minibatches rather than randomly permuted training rows, keeping all features and hyperparameters fixed.
rationale: The internal request-context screen showed positive lift on each of the four late training-only holdout dates, but daily variability was material. Chronological optimization may better preserve temporal drift in the learned context effects, though it can increase recency bias.
exact_ablation: Change only the training-row order from seeded random permutation each epoch to chronological date/source order; retain request-context features, BCE, additive architecture, batch size, learning rate, epoch count, and checkpoint rule.

expected_effect.GAUC: Small uncertain effect, approximately -0.002 to +0.004; temporal alignment may help late users but reduce averaging over older patterns.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral to small positive, approximately -0.002 to +0.004, with possible late-period improvement and early-period regression.

text: Use user-contiguous minibatches for BCE so each update contains multiple impressions from the same users, without changing the pointwise objective.
rationale: Official metrics depend on within-user ordering, while the current pointwise training batches are randomly mixed. User-contiguous batches may provide more coherent gradient updates for user-specific ranking, although the additive model still cannot learn explicit pairwise interactions.
exact_ablation: Change only minibatch construction from random row batches to batches formed by complete or near-complete user blocks; retain BCE, features, additive architecture, optimizer, schedule, and total training rows fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Possible small positive effect of approximately +0.000 to +0.004 from more coherent user updates, but it may be unchanged because BCE remains pointwise.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Possible small positive effect of approximately -0.001 to +0.004; large users may dominate updates and hurt sparse users.

text: Replace full within-user pair construction with one hard-negative pair per positive, selected from the highest-scoring negatives in each training batch.
rationale: The pairwise loss experiment underperformed its parent, but its implementation used all positive-negative pairs and had materially different score behavior. Hard-negative selection is a distinct pairwise training ablation that concentrates updates on ranking errors likely to affect the head.
exact_ablation: Change only pair construction within the existing pairwise-loss model from all within-user positive-negative pairs to one highest-current-score negative per positive within each batch; keep request-context features, additive architecture, optimizer, schedule, and checkpoint rule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Potential recovery or small lift of approximately -0.001 to +0.005 relative to experiment 2, if difficult pairs improve ordering; unstable batches may hurt GAUC.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Potentially positive by approximately +0.001 to +0.007 because hard negatives are near the ranking boundary, with risk of overfitting noisy negatives.

text: Add deterministic score-margin regularization to the existing within-user pairwise loss, penalizing positive-negative pairs whose margin is below a fixed target.
rationale: Experiment 2 improved neither GAUC nor nDCG@5 relative to experiment 1, with GAUC 0.66592 and nDCG@5 0.53498. A margin term may increase separation among close pairs, but can distort the top-five ordering when the margin is too aggressive.
exact_ablation: Add only a fixed margin of 0.2 to the existing within-user pairwise logistic loss, replacing log(1+exp(-(s_positive-s_negative))) with log(1+exp(0.2-(s_positive-s_negative))); keep all features, architecture, optimizer, schedule, and pair set unchanged.

expected_effect.GAUC: Possible small positive effect of approximately +0.000 to +0.004 by separating ambiguous pairs, but margin pressure may amplify rare-item errors.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Uncertain effect, approximately -0.002 to +0.005; stronger margins can improve head separation or push noisy positives above relevant items.

text: Increase L2 regularization on the request-context embeddings while leaving the model architecture and training procedure unchanged.
rationale: Request context has positive train-only screening lift but experiment 1 shows severe weakness in sparse tabs and hours. Stronger regularization may reduce memorization of low-support context values and improve robustness, at the cost of shrinking a real signal.
exact_ablation: Change only context-field L2 from the baseline regularization to 10 times the baseline for tab, hour, and weekday parameters; keep user/video parameters, features, BCE, optimizer, schedule, and checkpoint rule fixed.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely neutral to small positive, approximately -0.002 to +0.003, if sparse context overfit is currently hurting broad ordering.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral or mildly positive, approximately -0.002 to +0.004, though excessive shrinkage can remove useful top-five context effects.

text: Remove weekday from the request-context group while retaining tab and hour, testing whether the weakly varying calendar signal adds noise to within-user ranking.
rationale: The request-context group was positive overall, but its aggregate evidence does not identify which field provides the gain, and hourly slices remain weak. Removing one context field is a clean feature ablation that may improve generalization if weekday effects are unstable while preserving the stronger tab/hour signals.
exact_ablation: Remove only the weekday feature from the current request-context scorer; retain user_id, video_id, tab, and hour with the same additive architecture, BCE objective, optimizer, schedule, and rows.

expected_effect.GAUC: Likely neutral to slightly negative, approximately -0.002 to +0.002, because weekday may contribute a small amount of broad ordering signal.
expected_effect.nDCG@5: Likely neutral, approximately -0.002 to +0.002; removing unstable calendar effects could help sparse contexts but may reduce top-five personalization.
